A day in the life of a welder
Where do they work?
A welder joins metal parts by melting them with heat. They work in workshops, factories, shipyards, on construction sites and on pipelines.
welding
Work order and drawing
The day starts with the work order and technical drawing: which parts, which joint and which method are read.
technical drawing
Preparation
The joint edges are ground, rust and oil are cleaned off, and the parts are aligned and tacked. Half of a good weld is preparation.
joint preparation
Welding
The electric arc melts the metal. The welder moves the torch or electrode at the right angle and speed to lay a smooth bead.
arc
Inspection
The weld is cleaned and checked by eye: are there pores, cracks or undercut? On important jobs, special testing is done.
quality control
How do you become one?

It's learned in the metal technology field of vocational high schools, on courses and alongside a master. In Türkiye, welding requires an MYK vocational qualification certificate; many projects also require a welder certificate.

Safety in welding
Welding helmet
Arc light burns the eyes and skin. Welding is done with a helmet that has a filter of suitable shade. Auto-darkening helmets darken by themselves when the arc strikes.
filter lens
Gloves are a must in welding
Unlike turning and milling, welding requires leather welding gloves: hot metal, sparks and arc light leave the hand unprotected otherwise.
leather gloves
Clothing
Flame-retardant work clothes, a leather apron and safety shoes are worn. Synthetic clothes melt with sparks and stick to the skin.
protective clothing
Fumes
Welding fumes are harmful to health. A fume extraction arm or good ventilation is used; you don't put your head in the fumes.
fume extraction
Fire
Flammables within about 10 metres of the welding area are removed or covered with a fireproof blanket. A fire extinguisher is kept ready.
fire precautions
Electricity
Cables must be intact, and gloves and shoes dry. No welding on wet ground or with damaged cables.
electric shock
Know the welding methods
Stick electrode
A coated stick electrode both strikes the arc and melts to become filler. Its coating protects the weld as it burns and leaves slag on top. The machine is simple and works outdoors too.
manual metal arc (stick) welding
MAG (gas-shielded)
Wire is fed continuously from a spool; Ar+CO₂ or CO₂ gas shields the weld from the air. It's fast; most steel work in workshops is done with it.
MAG welding
MIG
The same machine as MAG, but the shielding gas is an inert gas such as argon. Used on metals such as aluminium.
MIG welding
TIG
The arc burns from a non-consumable tungsten electrode, filler wire is added by hand, and the gas is argon. It's slow but gives a very clean, precise weld.
TIG welding
Oxy-fuel
An oxygen and acetylene flame melts the metal. Today it's mostly used for cutting, heating and repairs.
oxy-acetylene
Earth clamp
The welding circuit is completed with the earth clamp. The clamp is attached firmly to a clean spot on the part or the welding table.
earth / ground

Make a butt weld
You're going to join two steel sheets end to end with gas-shielded (MAG) welding. Do the steps in the right order.
Put on your glasses, grind the sheet edges and clean off rust and oil
Clean metal fuses smoothly; rust and oil cause porosity.
First the surface must be ready.
Align the sheets leaving a root gap, attach the earth clamp
The gap lets the fusion reach the bottom; the earth clamp completes the circuit.
The parts are clean; now position them.
Open the gas, set the gas flow and current, put on your helmet and gloves
The gas shields the weld from the air; the settings decide the weld quality.
The parts are in place; prepare the machine.
Tack both ends
Tacks hold the parts so the gap doesn't close during welding and the sheet doesn't distort.
Everything is set; first fix the parts in place.
Hold the torch at the right angle and run the weld at an even speed
A steady speed and angle give an even, smooth weld.
The parts are tacked; now the main weld.
Clean the weld with a wire brush and inspect it by eye
Pores, cracks and undercut can be seen on a clean surface.
The weld is done; is it good?
Butt weld order
Clean → align and earth → gas, current, helmet → tack → weld → inspect.
The root gap lets the weld fuse right to the bottom.
Tacks prevent distortion.

Settings and hand skill
Current
Current decides how much the metal melts. At low current the metal doesn't fuse well; at high current the edges burn and spatter increases.
welding current
Electrode diameter
A rough rule: about 30–40 amps for each millimetre of electrode diameter. The actual value is written on the electrode box.
current range
Angle
The electrode or torch is held slightly tilted relative to the direction of travel. If the angle is off, the weld drifts to one side.
torch angle
Speed
If you go too fast, the weld stays thin and doesn't fuse to the bottom; too slow and it piles up and overflows.
travel speed
Weld appearance
A good weld has an even width and regular ripples; there are no grooves at the edges and no holes on top.
weld bead

Try the settings first on a scrap piece of the same thickness. Don't use the job as a test.

Master-level topics
Welding positions
Flat (PA), horizontal fillet (PB), horizontal (PC), vertical up (PF), vertical down (PG), overhead (PE). In difficult positions the molten metal wants to run; the master controls it.
position
Weld preparation
Thick plate doesn't fuse to the bottom in one pass. A V-shaped groove is cut at the edges, leaving a root gap and root face.
V-groove
Multi-pass welding
First the root pass, then the fill passes, and finally the cap pass. Each pass is cleaned.
root, fill, cap
Preheating
With thick or some alloy steels, the part is heated before welding. This reduces fast cooling and the risk of cracking.
preheat
Distortion
Heated metal expands, then shrinks as it cools and bends the part. Tacking, a balanced welding sequence and short welds reduce distortion.
distortion

On important jobs everything is written down: method, material, current, pass sequence. This is called a welding procedure specification (WPS).
